body.text: A legally registered entity exists and the submitted identity is the same one. The submitted name matches across all five state registrations, the submitted office address matches an address on a registration, and the entity type is consistent against the domestic filing, the four foreign filings, and all five read together. Three independent handles on the same company agree.

It is active where it says it operates. Two of the five filings are active, one is inactive, and two return no status at all — a spread that reads as a company registering where it does business rather than as decay, because the active one includes the state of the submitted office address.

The one status that cannot be read is the formation state's. Delaware returns no status for the domestic filing and publishes no good-standing sub-status, so the registration a reader would most want confirmed is the one the record cannot speak to.
The company's own website corroborates the submitted identity independently of the registries — the business name, the office address and the submitted email address all match what the site carries.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware domestic registration is active and in good standing
gaps.wouldAnswer: Delaware publishes neither a status nor a good-standing sub-status through this channel, so no order returns one. A Certificate of Good Standing obtained from the customer is the only route.

gaps.point: Which two filings return no status, and whether either has lapsed
gaps.wouldAnswer: Two of the five states returned no status. Re-running the registration search would resolve them; until then "two active" is a floor rather than a full count.
